neighborhood_overview:
The studio is located in the 8th district of Lyon.

The pleasant neighborhood of Monplaisir is famous for its impressive Lumière museum, which traces the history of the seventh art. The Lumière Institute, with its particular architecture, presents art and experimental productions. This green and friendly neighborhood, with its village atmosphere, is full of wine shops, cheese shops and chocolate shops. Its market is an institution in Monplaisir (Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays). You will find charming restaurants as well as all the amenities.

You will find a supermarket 3 minutes away, and several others within 10 minutes. For longer stays, we also recommend excellent farmers' markets and shops direct from the producers.

Places to visit:
- The Parc de la Tête d'Or.
- The Museum of Confluences.
- The Basilica of Notre Dame de Fourvière.
- The Museum of Fine Arts of Lyon.
- The Saint-Jean-Baptiste cathedral.

Chic & Bohemian, the Croix-Rousse is a charming neighborhood of Lyon.

The Croix-Rousse is located north of thepeninsula. From the Terreaux or the Opéra de Lyon you can immediately climb the "slopes », then the "plateau »of the Croix-Rousse (where the apartment is located). There is a village atmosphere, a little bobo and very nice.

You will find small craft shops (Lyon designers: jewelry, accessories, clothing, etc.) and the most beautiful terraces in Lyon.

Silky or « canuts » once lived and worked in this neighborhood, Lyon being the capital of silk.

It is on the slopes that there are many authentic Lyon stoppers. And yes, the first customers of the corks were the canuts, who came to support themselves with the Lyon mothers, from a family kitchen. It is because of this workers' past that the hill of the Croix-Rousse is called «the hill that works» as opposed to Fourvière «the hill that prays».

neighborhood_overview:
The Croix-Rousse district in Lyon is the hill that prolongs the Peninsula to the north between the Saône river and the Rhône river. It is composed of two distinctive quarters: the flat top of the hill (Le plateau) where the apartment is located and the slopes (les pentes) . It is the mixture of these two that make it a vibrant quarter: a village atmosphere on the plateau with its famous Farmers market on the weekend, Or artists, young designers shops and night-life on the slopes
Walk to the terrace overlooking the city (Gros Caillou, Bellevue or Grande Cote) and you'll enjoy a lovely view of Lyon. You can then walk down the pentes, enjoying the colorful buildings, narrow streets, and changing views of Lyon and then reach the center town (800 meters or ½ miles).
Coming back up: take the funicular (Metro C) from Hotel de Ville Station to La Croix Rousse Station

host_about:
I love travelling and as soon as I got to know and use Airbnb for my trips I've loved it! I find that it gives you the feeling that you are more than a tourist in a foreign city, you sort of share the life of the other citizens around and I really enjoy it. Lately I have decided to become a host myself, and this will be a new experience for me. I believe my own experience as a traveller and guest should help me.

I love meeting new people, sharing our experiences, discovering new things, other ways of living...
I do read a lot (amazing how much spare time people have for it when they don't have a tv set!). 
I am french but speak fluently english and spanish. I also know some italian and portuguese, but I must say I've never practiced them enough to be good at them. I also started to learn greek two years ago, it has been a bit of a fight sometimes, but I am in love with this language, country, culture, history. I only lack opportunities to practice it more often. 
I've also lived for some time in Peru few years ago, and I loved it. Such a different life from the one I've had in France until then, but this time is forever in my heart. 
And I've also still got in mind some wonderfull landscapes I've seen when I travelled to New Caledonia, which represents for me the image of paradise. I wish I will go back soon.
And among the other things I like to do, of course, I love to meet up with my friends. They are my second family. The one I chose like some say, even if I've never had the feeling I purposely chose them. My heart or my instinct chose them when life put them on my way, and they are truly very important to me.

Originaires et amoureux de notre ville, nous vous proposons une chambre dans notre appartement de 70m² situé dans le 6ème arrondissement de Lyon, proche de l'ancienne gare des Brotteaux.

Nous serions ravis de vous accueillir chez nous, et de nous rendre disponible pour vous recommander les meilleurs lieux à découvrir, les bons petits restau, ainsi que les bons plans du moment :)

Notre appartement se situe :
- à 5 minutes des deux métros les plus proche
- à 5 minutes de notre superbe Parc de la tête d'Or
- à moins de 15 minutes des Halles de Lyon et du Centre Commercial de la Part Dieu.
- à 20 minutes à pied de la Presqu'île

Le quartier des Brotteaux est un quartier dynamique, avec de nombreux commerces, épiceries, bars et restaurants.

Vous avez la possibilité de garer votre voiture dans les nombreuses rues ou se trouve pour les chanceux des places gratuites ! Si vous souhaitez plus de confort pour votre voiture des parkings payants souterrains sont également non loin de l'appartement.

Nous sommes situés entre les arrêts de métro MASSENA (ligne A) et BROTTEAUX (ligne B) --> 5 minutes à pieds montre en main ;)

La ligne B vous donnera un accès rapide à la gare et au centre commercial de la Part Dieu (1 arrêt)

La Croix rousse est à seulement 4 arrêts de métro, et le Vieux Lyon à 5 arrêts !


Vous trouverez également non loin de l'appartement différentes stations Vélov' pour vos déplacements urbains à bicyclette ;) (très pratique pour se déplacer à Lyon à moindre coût!)

neighborhood_overview:
The Croix-Rousse, nicknamed "the hill that works" in reference to the canuts, is an original area, with a "village" spirit, deeply marked by its past as a high place of the silk industry.

The Red Cross is located north of the Peninsula. From the Terreaux or the Opera you can immediately climb on the "slopes ". On the plateau of the Croix Rousse, there is a village atmosphere, a little bobo and very nice.

This is where silks or " canuts " once lived and worked, Lyon being the silk capital. A working-class neighborhood, he was poor and ill-famous for a long time. This has changed a lot! It is on the slopes that we find many authentic Lyon corks. And yes, the first customers of the corks were the canuts, which came to support themselves with the Mothers of Lyon, from a family kitchen. It is because of this worker's past that the hill of the Red Cross is called " the hill that works " as opposed to Fourvière " the hill that prays ".

Take a walk on the Boule

neighborhood_overview:
Old Lyon is the medieval and Renaissance district of Lyon. It is located on the banks of the Saône, at the foot of the hill of Fourvière. This is one of the largest neighborhoods concerning this medieval and Renaissance period (with Venice) which has remained intact until today.

Walking around this historic site means strolling through time, from its foundation in 43 BC to the present day. The city has kept permanent and continuous traces of the periods that marked its history.

During the Renaissance, the peak period of the city, the three neighbourhoods that make up it take on their characteristics :
- Saint Paul in the North : district of the great bourgeoisie, financial and commercial center
- Saint John between the other two: district of the high clergy and aristocracy
- Saint-Georges in the South: craftsmen's district.

neighborhood_overview:
The lively 1st arrondissement centers around the majestic City Hall and 19th-century Bartholdi Fountain on Place des Terreaux. Cultural landmarks include the Lyon Museum of Fine Arts, with its Impressionist masterpieces, and the Lyon National Opera, designed by Jean Nouvel. Indie bookshops and vinyl stores fill steep streets, and alfresco bistros line cobbled plazas. Hip, late-night music clubs fill Rue St. Catherine.

The plateau of Croix-Rousse, a haven of peace, is located 10 mins from the flat. Visit the renowned House of the Canuts, if you want to know everything about the history of Canuts and silk in Lyon.

The banks of the Saône is only 15 mins away on foot. While crossing the Saône, take a stroll to Vieux-Lyon (a historical site listed as a world heritage site by UNESCO).

Don’t forget to visit The Basilica of Fourvière which offers a stunning view of Lyon.

neighborhood_overview:
Welcome in Grange-Blanche Montchat, one of the oldest quarter of town. The nice castle of Montchat (XVIth century) was one of the residences of Christina, Queen of Sweden. Due to its history, Montchat has kept a homely atmosphere : we call it "the village in Lyon".
The neighborhood is quiet, mostly filled with families. There is a plenty of open areas and parks, of which the park Chambovet. It used to be the private garden (5 hectares) of René Tavernier, a French writer who hid the communists and famous writers Louis Aragon and Elsa Triolet during the war (1941-43). A workers gardening lot has been build in 1926 next to the park : from there you have a very nice viewpoint on the city.

Near to the city center, but friendlier and quieter, it is a very secure neighborhood even by night.

- Rue Mercière, vestiges of the Renaissance Presqu'île is home to remarkable 15th and 16th century buildings. It is now known for its large number of restaurants.

description:
35 m2 apartment, tastefully renovated, French ceiling, in the courtyard of an old building.
Combining the charm of the old with modern comforts, it is located in the heart of the historic and medieval center.
Ideal base to discover this lively neighborhood with many restaurants and shops and visit Lyon (on foot or by transport) and its must-see sites.

neighborhood_overview:
This historic district, typical, very lively and touristic, is ideal to discover Lyon on foot or by transport (subway, bus, vaporetto) and its gastronomy (many restaurants and Lyon stoppers).
You can stroll the winding and ancient streets, with the wrought facades, visit the famous Saint John Cathedral and stroll the twists and turns of the traboules.
The funicular will take you to Fourvière and will offer you stunning views of the city.
Bellecour and the Presqu'île (Terreaux, Cordeliers) are only a few steps (across the Saône, through the various bridges and footbridges) and will give you another face of Lyon with its wide bustling streets, Haussmann buildings and its magnificent Hôtel-Dieu.
From Les Terreaux, you can go to La Croix-Rousse and its slopes (another typical area) or relax with a bucolic walk to Parc de la Tête d 'Or.

The apartment is located in the 7th district.

The 7th district of Lyon is the largest district of the city. Along the Rhone river, it is a multifaceted area! Between its green spaces like the Blandan park, its numerous bicycle paths allowing to cross the district by bike but also its numerous cafés and restaurants , it is a neighbourhood where one is never bored! You will also be a few minutes away from the Part-Dieu district, which is considered as the second city centre of Lyon.

Parc Blandan (a former military fort transformed into a park) is our local park, about 5 minutes away. You can also reach Lyon’s more famous park, Parc de la tête d’Or, on foot or on the tram located across the street. I love my neighborhood! I would live in no other district in Lyon. It’s central, 15 min walk from the extra centre, but gives you the feeling of a busy village of the South. I always feel in holiday here.

Ever since the 19th century, the Croix-Rousse district has been known as "the hill that works", while the Fourvière district, was baptised "the hill that prays". The Croix-Rousse was formerly the neighbourhood of Lyon's silk manufacturers, and during the 19th century it reverberated with the sounds of the "bistanclaques", an onomatopoeic name given to the weaving looms by the inhabitants of the city.

With 30,000 canuts (name given to the silk workers in Lyon) the district was a hive of activity, and the city itself a major hub for textiles in Europe. Modern-day visitors are invited to stroll through the area to discover its true essence and the many colored buildings specially built to house the weaving looms, amid a maze of traboules and stairwells. Your home away from home in the beautiful city of Lyon!

Enjoy all the creature comforts you're used to in the best neighborhood in Lyon - just blocks from the Opera House and metro station Hotel de Ville without the walk up the hill to Croix Rousse or the touristy, crowded areas of the Old Lyon. Historic buildings, unique culinary restaurants, record stores, and specialty food markets abound. The vibe is young but loud bars and clubs are few if any. Place de Terreaux, the Opera House, the beautiful Paroisse Saint-Polycarpe church, and Hotel de Ville are minutes away by foot. And the Croix Rousse neighborhood (with unique shops, the silk museum, artists' workshops and much more) is just up the hill by foot or metro (one stop away).
host_about:
I am an American in France (I moved here to be with my French husband, Pierre). My hometown (of 26 years) is Atlanta, Georgia but I’ve fallen so in love with France, I plan to stay forever. 

I'm a xenophile and a former Couchsurfer so my desire is to share experiences with people from all over the world.  When I travel,  I don't follow an itinerary or list of sites to see, as I prefer to just be in the place I'm visiting and pretend like I'm a local (as much as that is possible).  I also most enjoy meeting people wherever I go so that I feel connected to places through the people that live there.

Lyoners will tell you, the Point du Jour is a "apart" neighborhood either unknown or acclaimed by its fans who would not move for anything in the world! Located in the 1st arrondissement of Lyon, the district extends from the plant garden to the top of the hill of Croix-Rousse . It is the famous passage between the city of Lyon and the village of Croix-Rousse. With its hills, many stairs, colorful canut buildings, the walk is full of charm !

The neighborhood revolves around the Montée de La Grand-Côte, which almost vertically connects Place des Terreaux to Boulevard de la Croix-Rousse. To the west is the Chartreux district with its gardens overlooking the Saône. To the east, the ascent of San Sebastian, the Esplanade du Gros Caillou and Place Bellevue offer magnificent views of the Parc de la Tête d 'Or and the Alps.

The apartment is 15 meters from the Esplanade du Big Pebou !

A large market is held on the Boulevard de la Croix-Rousse, from Tuesday to Sunday (plus organic market on Saturdays) where the producers of the region come.

It is also a very lively area with many terrace bars and restaurants.

Virginia, my co-host, also lives in the neighborhood and can advise you during your stay.

Je m’appelle Mary. J’aime les voyages, la nature et la spiritualité.

Je suis particulièrement attachée à ces passions.

En voyage, j’aime faire de nouvelles rencontres, échanger avec des personnes aimant leur territoire et partager leur quotidien (coutumes, traditions….).

Mary.

neighborhood_overview:
Description of the Vieux Lyon neighborhood
is the medieval and Renaissance district of Lyon. It is located on the edge of the Saone, at the foot of the Fourvière hill. It is one of the most extensive neighborhoods concerning this medieval and Renaissance period (with Venice) that has remained intact until today.

Walking around this historic site means strolling through time, from its foundation in 43 BC to the present day. The city has kept permanent and continuous traces of the periods that have marked its history.

During the Renaissance, when the city reached its peak, the three districts that make up the city took on their characteristics :
- Saint-Paul in the North: Grand Bourgeoisie district, financial and commercial center
- Saint-Jean between the other two: High Clerk and Aristocracy district
- Saint George to the south: neighborhood of artisans.

In 1862, the world's first urban funicular was in service between Rue Terme and Boulevard de la Croix-Rousse.
In 1891, a second funicular was put into service between Croix-Paquet and Croix-Rousse. The first funicular was converted into a road tunnel after it was closed in 1967.

Chic and bohemian, Croix Rousse is an endearing neighborhood in Lyon. Here you will find small shops, Lyonese traffic jams, a nice market, and a village atmosphere.

The Croix Rousse is located north of the Presqu'île. From the Terreaux or the Opera you can immediately climb on “the slopes”. On the Croix Rousse plateau, there is a very pleasant village atmosphere.

It is in this district that once lived and worked the silks or "canuts", Lyon being the capital of silk. A working-class district, he was poor and ill-famed for a long time. That has changed a lot! It is on the slopes that we find many authentic Lyon corks. And yes, the first customers of the corks were the canuts, who came to support themselves with the Mères Lyonnaises, a family kitchen. It is because of this working-class past that the hill of Croix Rousse is called "the hill that works" as opposed to Fourvière "the hill that prays".

neighborhood_overview:

La Croix Rousse is located on the north of the Presqu'île. From Les Terreaux or the Opéra, you can immediately climb on "the slopes". On the Croix-Rousse plateau, it reigns a village atmosphere, a little bobo and very pleasant.

This is where silks or " canuts " once lived and worked, Lyon being the silk capital. A working-class neighborhood, he was poor and ill-famous for a long time. This has changed a lot! It is on the slopes that we find many authentic Lyon corks. And yes, the first customers of the corks were the canuts, which came to support themselves with the Mothers of Lyon, from a family kitchen. It is because of this worker's past that the hill of the Red Cross is called " the hill that works " as opposed to Fourvière " the hill that prays ".

neighborhood_overview: History of the Ainay district. Situated south of Place Bellecour, this area is made up of dwellings mostly dating back to the 19th century. It developed around the Basilica of St. Martin-d 'Ainay, a testament to Roman art, built in the 11th century under the Restoration. This religious estate was surrounded by ramparts, which can still be seen. The rich silks settle in the 18th century and traditionally the large Lyonese families invest in the vast old apartments. While the facades remain non-esthetic, the richness should remain discreet, the interiors reflect the hidden gems of the time. (Source Barnes)

neighborhood_overview: History of the Ainay district. A favorite district of the Lyon aristocracy from the 18th century and the big bourgeoisie in the 19th, this small piece of Presqu'île has been able to transform while retaining its soul. Located south of Place Bellecour, this district is made up of dwellings dating mostly from the 19th century. It developed around the basilica of Saint-Martin-d'Ainay, a testimony of Romanesque art, built in the 11th century under the Restoration. This religious estate was surrounded by ramparts, traces of which can still be found. The rich silks settled there in the 18th century and traditionally the large Lyon families invested the vast old apartments. If the facades remain non-ostentatious, the wealth should remain discreet, the interiors reflect the hidden splendors of the time. (Source Barnes)

Central area and ideal for travellers interested in architecture, art and cuisine. 15 minutes walk from Place Bellecour and 5 minutes from Place des Terreaux.
The historic heart of the city of Lyon, you can discover the famous traboules and cobbled streets, Gallo-Roman remains. An attractive and very commercial district, the streets are lined with Lyon's "bouchons" where you can discover the specialities and finish the evening in one of the many bars. Stroll through the narrow streets dotted with sights and museums, not forgetting Saint Jean Cathedral, a must-see in Vieux Lyon. You can also see the Church of Saint Georges and Saint Paul. Just take the funicular to visit the Basilica of Fourvière, which overlooks the city and offers a breathtaking view. neighborhood_overview:
The slopes of Croix-Rousse is located between the Croix-Rousse district and Place des Terreaux / Hôtel de Ville, it is a lively and pleasant neighborhood. You will enjoy small shops such as lively bars, Lyon restaurants/traffic jams, cafes/brunch, cafes/brunch, cafes/theaters, thrift stores, … The students and artists give the neighborhood this bohemian atmosphere.

Thanks to its rich history, the district has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998.

In the 17th and 18th centuries were on the slopes, many gardens and convents. It is from the 18th century that the neighborhood begins to host the canut workshops, silk workers who until then worked in Old Lyon. They installed their workshops and dwellings on the slopes and in the Croix-Rousse district in buildings designed to contain their important looms. These immense places of life have many characteristics of their own that today make all the charm of the architecture of the neighborhood.

neighborhood_overview:
The Croix Rousse district is known for its quality of life in Lyon. A village spirit (quite Bobo, you have to admit it) full of charm and very "safe"!
Although the neighborhood is very quiet at night, there are many quality bars and restaurants. (Especially towards Place des Tapis)
Several times a week you will find a large farmers market on Boulevard de la Croix-Rousse.
The small streets of the plateau swarm with small, super nice independent shops! (Shops, bookstores, decor shop, gifts, clothes, etc.)
As a bonus, you can choose to walk down the hill to reach the city center. You will cross the "slopes" which are also an iconic area of Lyon. Many street artists, artisans, small creators and other independent shops have taken up residence! Not to mention the bars and restaurants that abound on the slopes!

Walk its cobblestone streets and discover the artistic hustle and bustle that reigns here. The traboules, secret passages typical of Lyon, will guide you through charming courtyards and picturesque stairs. La Croix-Rousse is full of craft shops, art galleries, and lively cafes, creating a bohemian vibe where art and creativity are in the spotlight.

neighborhood_overview:
Located on the heights of the 5th arrondissement of Lyon, between the hill of Fourvière and the municipality of Sainte-Foy-lès-Lyon, the Point-du-Jour is a singular neighborhood, an enclave that claims its independence and its spirit of "village" in the city.

For the small historical reminder, the Point-du-Jour was the rallying point for hunting. On the location of the current Benedict Tessier square, the hunters met at dawn and therefore at the point of day to then head west.
